thread:
maya: Heads up — after the kernel/kernel-simd change landed to canary, p95 token latency jumped ~18% on the 8k benchmark. Not happy.
devin: Confirmed on my run earlier, p50 fine but p95 tail moved. I triggered a compare job: `./bench compare --canary canary-2026-03-01 --baseline stable-2026-02-28` and logs attached.
andre: Can you paste the exact histogram or numbers? Need to decide gate status for the release pipeline.
maya: Quick paste: baseline p95=220ms, canary p95=260ms. p99 moved from 480ms -> 620ms. Throughput unchanged.
sasha: Any evidence it's traffic-shape dependent? Did you run with KV cache warm vs cold?
devin: Ran both. Cold cache amplified the regression (p95 ~+28%). Warm still worse than baseline but smaller.
maya: Stack traces point at the new attention kernel in the runtime, likely changed memory access patterns causing more stalls. I'm starting a profile with perf and nvprof.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment canary-2026-03-01 completed at 1764999900. Health checks passed.
andre: Given numbers we should hold the canary gate. Need an approval to rollback to stable-2026-02-28 or patch the kernel. Opinions?
maya: My vote: rollback. We can't risk customer-facing regressions at p95/p99 even if avg is fine.
sasha: Agree rollback unless devin can show a targeted patch in next 2 hours that reduces tail. Can we pin the kernel to the old kernel build quickly?
devin: I have a quick revert candidate that flips back to old simd path when sequence_len>2048. Patch PR: https://git.internal/r/runtime/PR/4823 — CI is green locally but still running infra tests.
andre: If PR lands and we can validate perf on a canary run in <1h, we can avoid full rollback. But we need explicit approval from release lead.
maya: @andre you are release lead today — what's your call?
andre: I'm inclined to give 45 minutes for the targeted PR approach. If we don't see p95 within 10% of baseline by then, we rollback.
sasha: I'll queue a controlled rollback run plan in case — steps + contacts:
- ops: start rollback to stable-2026-02-28 (k8s label `canary=stable`) — ETA 20m
- eng-runtime: validate with `./bench smoke --suite=8k --warm` job id will be posted
- oncall: monitor customer-facing errors and latency dashboards
maya: I'll keep profiling in parallel and post call stacks.
devin: Starting a canary-run now with the patch flag: `BIN=runtime_canary ./bench run --canary --warm`. Posting results in ~18m.
ops-bot: perf-bot: scheduled bench job 1765000100 for `8k-warm`.
andre: Good. Everyone please react or ack. If you disagree with the 45min window speak now.
sasha: :thumbsup:
maya: :thumbsup:
devin: :thumbsup:
ops-bot: deploy-bot: if rollback triggered, I'll announce and run the rollback playbook.
maya: Noted. I'll update this thread as soon as I have profiler snapshots. If PR passes perf check we'll gate the revert to a canary-only toggle first.
devin: Bench result: baseline p95=219ms, patch p95=226ms, p99=501ms — within 3% of baseline. Uploading flame graphs.
maya: Flame graph looks cleaner; spike in memcpy removed. This is promising.
andre: Given that, I approve landing the patch and continuing canary. No rollback. We'll keep a watch window 3h post-merge.
sasha: I'll set the dashboard alert thresholds to tighter for the watch window and enable verbose tracing for the canary nodes.
maya: Thanks all. Closing the hold. ops-bot please annotate the canary release notes with the fix.
ops-bot: note-bot: annotated canary-2026-03-01 with patch PR/4823 and perf comparison.
